rv.q: Her duets with Cumming under Gavin Whitworth’s musical direction are things of beauty.
It's a gentle, beautiful story with some cracking lines that the cast bring to life beautifully.
But to use the tragedy abruptly as a plot device feels crass.
I can't accept the facile artistic choice to graft on this tragedy, and to time the run of this production during the 25th anniversary of the attack.

Cumming and Henderson give such charming, moving performances, and while this is testament to their great talents as actors and Andrew Panton’s direction, the impact of the script and score cannot be denied.

cn.t: Critics find this intimate two-hander elevated by the star power and subtle performances of Alan Cumming and Shirley Henderson, though the musical itself is seen as fragile and flawed beneath its wonderful staging.
